title: The tipping bucket, fast and slow

data.source: Jang (2026), Laboratory calibration dataset for tipping-bucket rain gauges: manual burette vs automated device, Mendeley Data v5, doi:10.17632/czzzth6z26.5

claim_kind: retrodiction (published laboratory data; mapping frozen before the outcome was analysed)
prediction: The water a tipping bucket needs per tip is the same at 10 and at 100 mm of rain an hour: the slope of log(water per tip) on log(rate) has a 95 % interval inside -0.05 to +0.05.
baseline: The field's own model (water arriving during the tip is lost, slope 0 to +0.04, from memory) and a clock decoy (a tip every fixed time, slope +1).
why: Water per tip stayed inside the band, but a small change with rate was resolved, so exact invariance is false and the field's leak model is the better description. The rise is about 8 % over the range; it is flat from 10 to 20 mm/h and then climbs, and over 20 to 100 mm/h alone the slope is only just inside the band.

amended.reason:
AMENDMENT, 2026-11-19, AFTER THE SECOND CHECK (docs/CHECKS_RATE_SECOND_LOOK.md). The frozen docstring, the verdict
and every first-run number are unchanged. Two things are added at the second checker's request. (1) The rise in
water per tip is "about 8 %": 8.41 % is the fitted slope carried across the range; the raw setting means are also
reported. (2) The slope is not one straight line: flat from 10 to 20 mm/h, then rising. The slope over the upper
four settings alone (20 to 100 mm/h) is reported; it is only just inside the band. So the pass depends on the
range as well as on the band.
